c.tagline: The world's smallest capital, wrapped in turf roofs and fog

card: Extremely card-friendly — contactless and chip cards are accepted almost everywhere, including small cafés, public restrooms, and buses; cash (Faroese krónur or Danish kroner) is rarely needed.
rides: Taxi.fo (local taxi company with online/phone booking)

taxi.color: Unmarked private sedans/minivans (no standard livery color)
taxi.fare: ~$15-20 for a short ride within central Tórshavn
taxi.fareNote: Metered fares in town; airport transfers to/from Vágar are typically flat-rate, around $100-130 for the 45-minute trip

emergency.note: Landssjúkrahúsið (National Hospital) is in Tórshavn; 112 covers police, fire, and ambulance for the entire country

religion: Evangelical Lutheran (Church of the Faroe Islands) ~80%

english.label: Easy to get by in English

walk: Central Tórshavn — Tinganes, the harbor, Reyn, and Vaglið — is compact and fully walkable in 20-30 minutes end to end, though streets are hilly and cobbled. Outlying highlights like Kirkjubøur, Saksun, Vestmanna, Gásadalur, and Mykines require a rental car, guided tour, or the SSL bus/ferry network.

safety.safety: Extremely safe — consistently ranks among the safest capitals in the world; violent crime is virtually nonexistent and police are unarmed.
safety.crime: Petty theft and pickpocketing are rare; locals often leave doors and bikes unlocked. The real risks for visitors are weather- and terrain-related — sudden fog, strong winds, and unfenced sea cliffs — rather than crime.

hood_landmark.Tinganes & Reyn (Old Town): Tinganes peninsula and Tórshavn Cathedral (Havnar Kirkja)
hood_landmark.Undir Ryggi: Harborside bar strip near Vestara Bryggja
hood_landmark.Vaglið: Vaglið square and the Niels Finsens gøta shopping street
hood_landmark.Viðarlund: Viðarlund town park and the National Gallery of the Faroe Islands
hood_landmark.Argir: Argir Church (Argir kirkja) and the seaside promenade

hood_desc: The postcard heart of the city — turf-roofed black wooden buildings housing the Faroese parliament (Løgting), narrow lanes, and a working harbor where fishing boats moor beside government ministries.
A tightly packed cluster of pubs, cafés, and late-night bars just above the harbor — the closest thing Tórshavn has to a nightlife strip, lively on weekends.
The pedestrian square and main shopping street, lined with boutiques, bakeries, and cafés; the natural gathering point in the city center.
A leafy park and cultural pocket a short walk from downtown, with duck ponds, walking paths, and the country's national art gallery.
A quiet residential suburb across the fjord from downtown, popular with families, with a seafront path connecting back to central Tórshavn.

water.note: Tap water is pristine and safe throughout the Faroe Islands.

transit.sys: Bussleiðin (free local city buses within Tórshavn) plus the national SSL bus and ferry network (Strandfaraskip Landsins)
transit.hours: Local buses run roughly 6:30am-11:30pm on weekdays with reduced weekend service; national SSL routes vary by line
transit.pay: Local Tórshavn city buses are entirely FREE — no ticket needed; national SSL buses and ferries charge fares (roughly $3-25 depending on distance), payable by card or the App SSL
transit.map: Route maps and schedules at torshavn.fo and ssl.fo
transit.note: There are no trains. A rental car or organized tour is generally needed to reach outlying villages and trailheads not served by bus, such as Saksun and Gásadalur.

transport.air: Vágar Airport (FAE) is the only airport in the Faroe Islands, about 45 minutes by car or bus from Tórshavn. Atlantic Airways and partner carriers fly from Copenhagen, Billund, Reykjavík, Edinburgh, Bergen, and other seasonal hubs.
transport.train: None — the Faroe Islands have no railway network.
transport.bus: SSL long-distance buses link all major towns via a network of undersea tunnels and bridges; local Tórshavn city buses are free to ride.
transport.ferry: Smyril Line's MS Norröna sails weekly between Hirtshals, Denmark and Tórshavn (about 2 days), continuing on to Seyðisfjörður, Iceland; domestic SSL ferries connect outer islands such as Nólsoy, Hestur, Sandoy, and Suðuroy.
transport.car: Rental cars are available at Vágar Airport and in Tórshavn; roads are well maintained but many routes pass through single-lane or toll subsea tunnels, so GPS or offline maps are recommended.

airport.name: Vágar Airport
airport.distance: ~30 mi (48 km) from Tórshavn, about 45 minutes by car or bus
airport.transport: SSL Bus 300 connects Vágar Airport to Tórshavn (~$12-15, about 1 hour with stops); taxi transfer runs ~$100-130; rental car counters (Avis, Europcar, 62N and others) are available at the airport terminal

net.m: Föroya Tele and Hey (Vodafone) sell tourist SIM cards for about $25-35, available at the airport and shops in Tórshavn
net.w: Free WiFi is common in cafés, hotels, and the public library; coverage is patchier in remote villages
net.ops: Föroya Tele, Hey, and Nema are the main mobile operators
net.gb: Prepaid tourist SIMs typically offer 5-20GB for around $25-40
net.fwn: 4G/LTE covers Tórshavn and the main road network reliably; signal can drop inside subsea tunnels and on remote hiking trails such as Mykines and Kalsoy
net.ap: eSIMs from Föroya Tele or international providers (Airalo, Holafly) can be activated before arrival

tip.s: No tipping is expected for services such as taxis or hotel staff — prices already reflect fair wages.
tip.r: Rounding up the bill or leaving 5-10% for exceptional service is appreciated but never required, even at destination restaurants like KOKS.
